### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**7** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **15** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 33b6e8bece79e70156dc2c1880813f8d88af61d4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `32e100a77d354e23e4414d0c94e2572e3388f4ff` — the merge of head `daf0aa882a4ab74f46758f4100b85dc94478edad` into base `33b6e8bece79e70156dc2c1880813f8d88af61d4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh

git fetch origin 32e100a77d354e23e4414d0c94e2572e3388f4ff && git checkout 32e100a77d354e23e4414d0c94e2572e3388f4ff
```

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `daf0aa882a4ab74f46758f4100b85dc94478edad`
Local-runs: none

PR objectstack-ai/objectstack#20904 (draft, `Part of #18386`), head `daf0aa882a` = merge of `origin/main` `33b6e8bece` into `cc2615825f`; merge base with `main` is `33b6e8bece`, so the net diff is exactly the PR's four files: `packages/rest/src/import-template.ts` (+87/-7), `packages/rest/src/import-template.test.ts` (+90), `packages/rest/src/import-template-route.test.ts` (+124), `.changeset/18386-template-required-option-default.md` (+12). Inputs read: the card body and all 20 comments (readings `5914688255`, claim `5914714137`, dev report `5915980985`, seat ruling `5916009192`), the PR body and file list, the net diff, the engine and validator at this head, and the head's check-runs. Nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**The predicate, judged case by case against the engine at this head.** `isTemplateRequired` (import-template.ts) now answers: not `required === true` → false; `system === true` / `readonly === true` / `type === 'autonumber'` → false; otherwise starred exactly when `templateInsertDefault(def)` is empty for `required`. Each leg against the engine:

- `defaultValue` present and not null wins — RIGHT. `ObjectQL.applyFieldDefaults` (engine.ts:5789) gates on `f.defaultValue == null`, so `''` is a real default and `null` is none; the template's `def.defaultValue != null` is the same test.
- `defaultValue: null` → falls through to the option list — RIGHT (same gate; parity shape `default_value_null` refused, `default_value_null_option_default` accepted and stored `c`).
- option `default: true` on a single-valued field → first marked value; on a multi-valued field → every marked value as an array — RIGHT. `resolveOptionDefault` (engine.ts:5733) reads only the canonical `default === true`, skips an option whose `value` is undefined or null, ignores non-object options, and returns `marked` or `marked[0]` by `declaredMultiValued` (engine.ts:1441), which is `isMultiValueField({ type, multiple: multiple === true })` from `@objectstack/spec/data`. The template's `templateInsertDefault` calls the same spec predicate with the same two-key shape, so `multiselect`, `checkboxes`, `tags` and `select` + `multiple: true` agree by construction; `option_default_select_multiple` stores `['b']`, `option_default_multiselect` stores `['a','c']`, `option_default_first_wins` stores `a`.
- string options (`options: ['a','b']`) declare no default — RIGHT (both sides `continue` on a non-object entry).
- option default on a non-option type (`text` with `options`) fills — RIGHT; the engine is deliberately type-agnostic (its own docblock), and the parity shape `option_default_any_type` pins it.
- `''` default, and `[]` default on a multi-valued field, stay starred — RIGHT. The validator's `isEmptyForRequired` (record-validator.ts:301) is `isMissing` (undefined, null, or a string whose `trim()` is empty) or, for `isMultiValueField(def)`, an empty array; the template's private copy is the same three-clause test, trim included. A `''` default on a non-text stored type reaches `null` through `normalizeBlankTypedValues` (record-validator.ts:642) and is refused the same way.
- `system` / `readonly` / `autonumber` never starred — RIGHT. `validateRecord` in insert mode skips `def.system || def.readonly` (record-validator.ts:1706) and `validateOne` exempts `autonumber` from the required check (record-validator.ts:885). Without `?fields=`, `templateColumns` already drops all three through `TEMPLATE_COLUMN_EXCLUSIONS`, so the exemption is reachable only through an explicit `?fields=` list — exactly what the code comment says, and what makes the instructions sentence hold for a starred `?fields=` column (before this PR such a column was starred while the import accepted its blank).
- Strictness: the template tests `=== true` where the validator tests truthiness (`def.system || def.readonly`, `def.required`). Equal for Zod-parsed registry metadata, where these keys are booleans; recorded as a spelling difference, not a drift.
- The schema the predicate reads is the registry object after `translateMetaItem` → `translateMetadataDocument` → `translateObject` (i18n-resolver.ts:2767), which copies each field as `{ ...def }` and each option as `{ ...opt, label }`: `defaultValue`, `required`, `system`, `readonly`, `type`, `multiple` and every option's `default` survive a zh-CN request. RIGHT — no localization drift.

**What metadata cannot see (the converse).** "Starred exactly when the import refuses a blank" holds in the starred ⇒ refused direction for every metadata-declared default; the refused ⇒ starred direction has four exceptions, none introduced by this PR: (a) a `before*` hook that fills the field (starred, then accepted); (b) an expression default that fails to evaluate (engine leaves it unset with a `warn`, then refuses); (c) a `current_user` token default with no acting user (`if (execCtx?.userId != null)` at engine.ts, else unset, then refused); (d) a `requiredWhen` rule that holds at insert. The PR body's Acceptance notes name (a) and (b); (c) and (d) are unnamed. The load-bearing author-shown sentence claims only the first direction (below), so this is an over-breadth in the PR body and in the `isTemplateRequired` docblock ("exactly when"), true for static `required: true` plus declared defaults, on `main` when this lands.

**The parity test's power.** `import-template-route.test.ts` registers 19 objects (`pty_*`), reads each template through the real route with `?fields=f`, asserts the header star, the instructions `D5` Yes/No and `isTemplateRequired` agree, then sends `{ f: '' }` through the real `POST /data/:object/import`, requires `code: 'required'` on refusal, and on acceptance requires the stored value to equal `templateInsertDefault`'s prediction. The 19 shapes cover every leg above (plain, `defaultValue`, `false`, option default on select / first-wins / multiselect / select+multiple / non-option type, no marked option, marked option without value, non-canonical `'true'` flag, null, null+option, defaultValue beats option, `''`, `[]`, readonly, system, autonumber). It is a property test through the door the copy is copying, so a change on either side that moves any of these 19 verdicts is caught. The ablation numbers in the PR body (7 red / 81 green, 11 disagreements) are the dev's, not re-run here; they are internally consistent (11 = 5 option-default shapes + `null`/`''`/`[]` + readonly/system/autonumber). Not covered: a picklist-bound field (no options at this head, see ③), and the four converse cases above, which no metadata-only test can express.

**`errorTitle` cut.** `errorTitle: c.header.slice(0, 32)`, `error: c.howToFill.slice(0, 255)` via two new constants — RIGHT: 32 and 255 are Excel's data-validation dialog limits, the `error` cut existed before as a literal 255. The unit test pins a 46-character label to a 32-character title and a short title written whole. `slice` counts UTF-16 code units, as the PR body says.

**Instructions sheet, each sentence about starred columns against the new predicate.**
- EN "Columns marked * are required: a row that leaves one of them blank is refused." / ZH "带 * 的列为必填:其中任一列留空的行会被拒绝。" — TRUE for every starred column under the new predicate (the 19-shape parity is starred ⇒ refused with no disagreement); the one way it can fail is a `before*` hook that fills the field, which no metadata declares. This is what the machine verification `5914688255` found false on `showcase_task.status` (required, `backlog` marked `default: true` — confirmed at `examples/app-showcase/src/data/objects/task.object.ts:44-51`); with this diff that column is unstarred and the sentence holds.
- Required column `Yes`/`No` (`是`/`否`) is `c.required ? text.required : text.optional`, and `c.required` is the same predicate — the row for a required select with a marked option says `No`, pinned in both locales by the `describeTemplateColumns` test and at `D6` by the route test.
- The example-row note and the read-projection note are untouched and unaffected.

**Changeset `.changeset/18386-template-required-option-default.md`, sentence by sentence.** Title ("` *` only when the import refuses a row that leaves it blank"): true in the direction it claims, hook caveat aside. Bullet 1 (option `default: true` → no star, instructions say not required, blank imports as the marked option): TRUE, pinned by the TICKET route test (`['Title *','Status']`, `D6` = `No`, stored `backlog`). Bullet 2 (`defaultValue: null` now starred unless an option is marked; `''` and `[]` on a multi-valued field now starred): TRUE, and "now" is right — the old predicate `defaultValue === undefined` left all three unstarred. Bullet 3 (`system` / `readonly` / `autonumber` named in `?fields=` no longer starred): TRUE. Bullet 4 (title cut to 32, Excel's longest): TRUE. `Clause-②: no`: right, see ②.

**PR body, remaining sentences.** "`isTemplateRequired` used to read only `defaultValue`" TRUE. "treats `defaultValue: null` as no default, and never runs `required` on `system`, `readonly` or `autonumber` fields" TRUE (for autonumber the required clause is exempted inside `validateOne`). "private members of `ObjectQL`" TRUE (both declared `private`); "`@objectstack/objectql` is only a devDependency of `@objectstack/rest`" TRUE (`packages/rest/package.json` line 45 under `devDependencies` at line 41; `import-template.ts` is not re-exported from `src/index.ts`, and the package's only `exports` entry is `.`). "19 field shapes" TRUE. Pins TRUE. Local verification, gate counts and the eslint reasoning are the dev's claims; the head's check-runs are the verdict on them. Acceptance note on picklists: TRUE at this head — outside `packages/spec` no source file names `picklist` (only an engine comment), and the resolver's own comment says a picklist-bound field "is served with its list's options resolved onto it" while resolving nothing itself, so template and engine both see no options today; when resolution lands it must reach both, as the note says. UTF-16 note TRUE.

**Public surface.** Three new exports and two new optional keys on `TemplateFieldDef` are package-internal (not on the entry); no query parameter, header, status or error code moves; the fixed behaviour belongs to the `template=true` feature whose minor changeset is still unreleased on `origin/main`. No accept set moves.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/rest` `patch`, `Clause-②: no` — matches what the diff publishes: a bug fix inside an unreleased feature of a released package, no export added to the package entry, no surface widened or narrowed. The PR body carries the same `Clause-②: no` line. Right level.

Clause-②: no

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report `5915980985` (`os-dev-report`, status done):
- **Deviation — the `system` / `readonly` / `autonumber` exemption goes one step past the claim's wording.** ANSWERED: right, and required — without it a required `?fields=` column of those kinds is starred while the import accepts its blank, which is the exact defect class the round fixes; the parity shapes `readonly`, `system`, `autonumber` measure it. The seat accepted it in `5916009192`; this review agrees on its own reading of `validateRecord`.
- **`open_questions[0]` — the unreleased minor changeset `.changeset/18386-export-import-template.md` says "` *` after each field that is required and has no default value".** ANSWERED: A (leave it), with two edge cases recorded where that sentence is loose: a required field with `defaultValue: ''` (or `[]` on a multi-valued field) has a default value and is starred; a required `system` / `readonly` / `autonumber` field named in `?fields=` has no default value and is not starred. Both changesets sit in `.changeset/` on `origin/main` and compile into the same release, and the patch entry states each case; the file is outside this PR's surface. No edit owed here.
- **`out_of_scope_findings[0]` — picklist resolution must reach both the template's object read and the engine's schema.** Verified true at this head (no runtime resolution exists); the seat's `5916009192` routes it to #19519 by pointer. ESCALATED by that pointer; the parity test is the right place for a picklist shape.
- **`out_of_scope_findings[1]` — `before*` hooks and failing expression defaults.** ANSWERED: true; add to the same class a `current_user` default with no acting user (engine leaves it unset) and a `requiredWhen` rule — the instructions sentence claims only starred ⇒ refused, so none of these falsifies it.
- **`out_of_scope_findings[2]` — UTF-16 surrogate at the 32nd unit.** ANSWERED: true, unreachable by any shipped label; noted.

Card thread: the machine-verification risks 2 (showcase grants nobody `allowExport`, so no one can download the template there) and 3 (a zh-CN template imported under an `en` request answers `invalid_option`) in `5914688255` are outside this PR's file surface and were routed by the seat to a decision card and to objectui#9600; nothing in this diff changes either. The claim `5914714137` scope items 1-3 are each delivered and pinned. Acceptance 6 remains the re-run of the machine verification after landing, per the maintainer's 「A，机器验证通过就直接关卡」.

Check-runs on `daf0aa882a`, read last, 38 runs deduped to 34 names keeping the newest `started_at`: 29 `success`, 5 `skipped` (Auto Label, Build Docs, Check PR Size, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)), 0 failed, none still running. All seven required contexts are `success`: Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Dogfood Regression Gate, Build Core, Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), Governed Surface Queue Guard. Check Changeset and Part-of PR must not also close its card are `success`. Not governed (no governed path in the file list); 320 changed lines.
